This is a follow up to https://github.com/music-assistant/support/discussions/3790#discussioncomment-18059598 with the feedback that in fact this feature doesn't work on mobile phones viewing the music assistant web page, at least not the way most people consume it: portrait. There is simply no option to change playback speed.

You can reproduce this without a phone by playing something you want to change the speed of on a computer browser and then opening the full-page now playing view (with the current album art large and in the center): you will see a menu in the top-right that does NOT have a playback speed adjustment, so even on desktop, if you have the current media "full-screen" you cannot change the speed, but you have to use the arrow in the top-left corner to minimize the now playing info to the bottom of the screen and then you can use a menu option on the right side to adjust the speed.  

On mobile web -- in portrait -- (i.e. the way everyone in Home Assistant consumes music assistant), the ONLY menu available is the full-screen now playing menu, and since that menu does not have the controls to change playback speed, it seems impossible to do on mobile phones.
posts.title: Playback speed NOT adjustable on mobile web

### What happened?

Every track from the niconico (nicovideo) music provider fails with `track://<id> not found on provider nicovideo--xxxx`, and playback aborts with `no more tracks available`.

The track isn't the problem. niconico's watch API returns `null` for `viewer.existence.prefecture`, and the pinned `niconico.py-ma==2.1.0.post2` types that field as a non-optional `str`. Pydantic rejects the whole response, `get_watch_data()` returns `None`, and the provider reports the track as missing.

It is always **1 validation error** — `age` and `sex` validate fine, so `prefecture` is the only broken field.

### How to reproduce

1. Set up the niconico provider with a normal (non-premium) account.
2. Play any track — it fails. Every track fails.

Hitting the exact endpoint the library uses (`/watch/{id}?responseType=json`) while logged in returns:

```json
{"id": "<redacted>", "nickname": "<redacted>", "isPremium": false,
 "existence": {"age": 26, "prefecture": null, "sex": "unanswered"}}
```

The account's profile is filled in; niconico simply no longer returns a prefecture. That suggests a server-side change on niconico's end, so it likely affects every user of this provider.

###

MA will ALWAYS organize the local files genres according to it's internal genre catalog regardless.

Ex: "Rap" will aways be created as an alias to "Hip-Hop" during first scan

This will require users with carefully curated local genres to manually "promote to genre" every single local genre that is interpreted as an alias by MA. (This can be really painful)

There is no way to bypass that internal MA genre definitions / assignments and just have MA import ONLY the local ones AS-IS, as main genres.

**Solution**

Roon have an interesting setting where you can toggle on/off the "internal" system and make it use ONLY the genres within the tags

![image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/8f96c41b-2589-4ad1-8080-662f89a68580)

Source: [https://help.roonlabs.com/portal/en/kb/articles/genre-setting](https://help.roonlabs.com/portal/en/kb/articles/genre-setting)

A setting like this will be a life saver. 

Just import local genres found in tags as main genres without any intervention and classification.

Thanks for all the amazing work guys !

🎵 MA HTML Player – a lightweight web dashboard for Music Assistant (even on ancient tablets)

I built a single-file HTML/JS dashboard for Music Assistant that's designed to run on old, low-powered tablets — my original use case was an iPad 4 running iOS 9, which is too old for the default MA web interface.

🏠 Dead-simple setup if you run Home Assistant: drop the 3 files (HTML, config, icon) into your <config>/www/ folder — no separate web server needed. HA serves them automatically under /local/, so you just open http://<ha-ip>:8123/local/ma-dashboard.html on the tablet and you're done. (Works standalone too, off any static web server or even file://, if you don't run HA.)

Other highlights:

📦 Single file, no build step, no dependencies
🔌 Talks directly to the MA WebSocket API (no HA in the middle for control)
🎚️ Station-style player switcher, incl. grouping/ungrouping players and per-member volume control
🔍 Search across tracks, albums, artists, playlists, radio, podcasts & audiobooks, with full drill-down navigation (artist → albums/top tracks, album → tracks, etc.)
⭐ Library tab with favorites, add-to-playlist, action sheets
🌓 Dark/light mode + accent color picker
posts.title: MA HTML Player – a lightweight web dashboard for Music Assistant (even on ancient tablets)

posts.excerpt:
# Motivation

Music Assistant currently has excellent support for:

- Music Providers
- Player Providers

However, there is no generic concept for **Audio Input Providers**.

Many modern devices contain physical audio inputs:

- WiiM Amp / Amp Pro / Ultra
- HDMI ARC
- Analog Line In
- Optical In
- Bluetooth Input

These inputs are currently only usable inside the vendor ecosystem.

Example:

Turntable
    ↓
Phono preamp
    ↓
WiiM Amp Pro Line In

The WiiM digitizes the audio internally (48 kHz / 16 bit PCM) and can already distribute it to other WiiM devices.

What is missing is exposing this input as a Music Assistant Audio Source.

# Proposal

Introduce a new Provider type:

Audio Input Provider

which publishes one or more Sources:

- WiiM Line In
- WiiM HDMI ARC
- WiiM Optical In

These sources should behave like any other Music Assistant source and be routable to any player.

# Why this is useful

This would make it possible to:

- stream vinyl throughout the house
- distribute TV audio
- use physical inputs in automations
- route live audio to Sonos, Chromecast, Snapcast, etc.

instead of limiting them to a single vendor
posts.title: RFC: Audio Input Provider API (Capture Sources) with first implementation for WiiM Inputs

### What happened?

A track in my Apple Music library that is **greyed out (unplayable) in the Apple Music app itself** is reported by the Apple Music provider as `available: True`. MA queues it, attempts playback, and only finds out it is unplayable when Apple's `webPlayback` endpoint refuses it.

The cause is in `music_assistant/providers/apple_music/parsers.py`, `parse_track()` (~line 255):

```python
# Check availability: library tracks owned by user OR catalog items with playParams
is_library_track = is_library_id(track_id) and track_obj.get("type") == "library-songs"
has_play_params = attributes.get("playParams", {}).get("id") is not None
...
available=is_library_track or has_play_params,
```

For any `library-songs` object, `available` is `True` unconditionally — `playParams` is never consulted. Apple signals "this cannot be played" by omitting `playParams`, so the one signal that would identify an unplayable library track is discarded for exactly the objects where it matters.

`parse_album()` has the same shape a few lines earlier (`is_library_album or has_play_params`), so albums are likely affected the same way.

### Logs

Sanitized — provider instance IDs and library ide

### Problem

When a player is part of a synced group, a pause command received from that player can pause the entire group. This can come from a physical play/pause button or the native device application.

For some players, that behavior is undesirable. A local or accidental pause on one portable speaker should not necessarily stop playback everywhere. I am seeing this with a Sonos Move used from Music Assistant alongside a Sonos Port / synced group.

This is especially relevant to the group-control routing introduced in [server PR #4950](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/4950), which intentionally forwards physical controls from an AirPlay speaker to its active Sendspin group.

### Proposed behavior

Add a per-player setting for inbound transport commands while that player is synced or bridged into a group:

- **Propagate to group** — current behavior and default
- **Ignore** — discard play, pause, stop, previous, and next commands received from that player while grouped
- **Detach and apply locally** — remove that player from the group, then apply the command only to it

The setting should affect inbound transport commands only. Volume commands and normal group sync
posts.title: Per-player policy for transport commands from a synced group member

### Browser and operating system

Home Assistant Companion app on iOS (WKWebView), reaching Home Assistant over a plain `http://` internal URL on the LAN.

The same failure should reproduce in **any** browser whenever the MA frontend is served over `http://` — including desktop Safari against `http://<host>:8095`. It works correctly in Safari when MA is reached over `https://`.

### What happened?

In **Provider details**, the **Copy URI to clipboard** action shows the green success toast — **"URI copied to clipboard"** — but nothing is actually written to the clipboard. Pasting afterwards yields whatever was on the clipboard before.

The success toast is the important detail: **the copy fails silently while reporting success.** I suspect that is why this keeps getting reported and then closed as not-reproducible — a maintainer testing over HTTPS takes the `navigator.clipboard` path and it genuinely works, and a user on WebKit sees a green toast and can't tell the difference from the UI alone.

Workaround: open the frontend in Safari over HTTPS, where the copy works.

1. Serve the MA frontend over pl

## Current State

The library listing views (tracks, albums, artists, playlists) currently use a dropdown menu with submenu items for sorting. While functional, this approach has some UX limitations:

- Current sort is not immediately visible
- Requires 2 clicks to change sorting (menu → submenu item)
- Sort direction not visually indicated
- Hidden in a submenu alongside other actions

**Current implementation:** Dropdown with `mdi-sort` icon → submenu with all sort options

## Problem

When users want to explore their library in different ways (recently added, most played, by name, etc.), the current UI requires navigating through a submenu. Additionally:

- Current sort state is not immediately visible
- Sort direction is not visually indicated  
- Changing sort requires multiple clicks

Modern media players use more prominent sorting controls that make the current state clear at a glance and make changes quick when needed.

## Related Discussion

This proposal complements [#6004 - Global settings for display and sorting](https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/6004), which focuses on **default/persistent sorting preferences**. That discussion

Music Assistant supports genres internally — `genres` controller, genre library items, and `get_genre_tracks()` in the queue builder — and `music_assistant.play_media` will happily play a `library://genre/<id>` URI. But neither HA service can *resolve* a genre by name, so scripts and voice assistants can't reach them.

**`handle_get_library`** (`homeassistant/components/music_assistant/services.py`): the schema accepts it via `vol.Required(ATTR_MEDIA_TYPE): vol.Coerce(MediaType)` — `GENRE` is a valid enum member — but the handler's dispatch has no `GENRE` branch and falls through to `raise ServiceValidationError(f"Unsupported media type {media_type}")`.

**`search_library`** (`controllers/music.py`): dispatches on ARTIST/ALBUM/TRACK/PLAYLIST/RADIO/AUDIOBOOK/PODCAST. No GENRE branch, though `MediaType.ALL` includes `GENRE` — which makes it look supported.

**Impact:** "play some jazz" can't be implemented. A script has no way to turn a genre name into a URI, so the workaround is a hand-maintained name→id map baked into the script — which silently plays the *wrong* genre if ids are ever renumbered.

**Why it looks small:** playback already works. `get_genre_tracks()` exists and is wi
posts.title: HA integration: get_library and search reject media_type: genre despite genres being fully supported in core

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.9.10 (also reproduced on 2.9.9)

### How is the MA server installed?

Docker container (`ghcr.io/music-assistant/server:2.9.10`), `network_mode: host`, on a Debian 13 LXC.

### The problem

`CacheController.set()` fails with `TypeError: default serializer exceeds recursion limit`. The exception is raised inside a fire-and-forget `asyncio.Task`, so it surfaces only as `Error doing task: Task exception was never retrieved` and the server carries on. The cache entry is silently never written, and the error message never names the offending type — which makes the failure practically undiagnosable from logs alone.

posts.excerpt:
### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.9.10 (also confirmed present in 2.9.9)

### What version of the Home Assistant Integration have you got installed?

Latest (HA 2026.7.4, MA HAOS add-on)

### The problem

**A user-supplied custom `music_app_token` (Apple developer token) is silently overwritten with the bundled shared token whenever the bundled token validates successfully.**

In `music_assistant/providers/apple_music/__init__.py`, `get_config_entries()` does:

```python
async with (
    mass.http_session.get(
        "https://api.music.apple.com/v1/test",
        headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {MUSIC_APP_TOKEN}"},
        ...
    ) as response,
):
    if response.status == 200:
        values[CONF_MUSIC_APP_TOKEN] = f"{MUSIC_APP_TOKEN}"   # <-- unconditionally clobbers a stored custom token
        default_app_token_valid = True
```

Because the bundled token is almost always "valid" (it only tests for HTTP 200, not for rate-limit health), any custom developer token a user stores is reverted to the bundled one on the next config-entries load. The user has no indication this happened — the SECURE_STRING field is hidden when `default_app_token_valid` is true.
posts.title: Apple Music: custom music_app_token is silently overwritten by the bundled token whenever the bundled token validates (makes personal developer tokens unusable)

I'm running multiple Spotify connect plugins to advertise different speaker groups as different "devices" within Spotify. This generally works well, however there is a start-up race condition.

Each plugin wishes to advertise itself, and will first check that it's preferred port (38800) is available. If it is found unavailable, then a different port will be chosen (usually incremented by 1). However, during a restart of music assistant, both plugins check port 38800 is free (which it is), and then try to startup using that port - at which point only one succeeds and the other enters an error state.

Manually reloading the plugin fixes the issue until the next restart, as during the reload, the second plugin correctly identifies

Music Assistant is slow to start some radios. Typically, https://stream.levillage.org/canalb takes ~9s to start on my setup. It seems that 5s come from this issue https://trac.ffmpeg.org/ticket/8104. `ffmpeg` takes time to properly identify the stream. Typically, `vlc` does not suffer of this issue. You can compare:

    ffmpeg -i https://stream.levillage.org/canalb -f alsa default

with:

    vlc https://stream.levillage.org/canalb

One workaround is to pass the the format and the codec to ffmpeg:

    ffmpeg -f mp3 -acodec mp3 -i https://stream.levillage.org/canalb -f alsa default    

MA could provide a way to associate format and codec to radio stream in the library. Even better, MA could semi-automatically fill these values.

Latest stable (issue is server-side; integration not involved)

Yes

### The problem

When streaming to **Sendspin players** (sendspin-go `sendspin-player` v1.8.2 in daemon mode, Raspberry Pi receivers), the "stream lead" — how far ahead of server-now the first chunks are timestamped — **varies wildly between sessions on the same queue**, from **+2.2 s to −0.6 s**. A zero or negative lead means chunks are already at (or past) their play deadline when they leave the server.

Measured `Chunk #0` logs from the same player (Pi Zero 2 W, same queue, same evening):

```
21:39:52 Chunk #0: timestamp=332655351917µs, serverNow=332653184624µs, diff=2167293µs (2167.3ms)   <- healthy lead
21:42:16 Chunk #0: timestamp=332795841409µs, serverNow=332796413417µs, diff=-572008µs (-572.0ms)  <- NEGATIVE lead (after a regroup)
21:53:30 Chunk #0: timestamp=333471028736µs, serverNow=333471012914µs, diff=15822µs (15.8ms)      <- near-ze
posts.title: Sendspin: stream start lead varies wildly between sessions (+2.2s to -0.6s), causing client-side late-chunk drops

On a multi-user Music Assistant server (tested on 2.9.9), the **frontend/UI language** can only be set:

- per user (stored server-side in the user's `preferences.language`), or

### Problem

The Smart Playlist "Year" rule filters using the release year stored for the
album/track, which for compilations, "best of" albums, and reissues is the
reissue date — not the original recording/release year. This makes
decade-based smart playlists (e.g. "90s hits") unreliable for anything in
your library via a compilation.

Example: "Come Softly To Me" by The Fleetwoods, originally released in 1959
(Capitol Records), is in my library via the compilation "Come Softly To Me:
The Very Best Of The Fleetwoods" (1992, via Qobuz). A Smart Playlist rule
"Year: 1990-2000" picks it up, even though it's a 1959 track.

### Proposed solution

Add support for an "original release year" field (distinct from the
edition/compilation year) that the Smart Playlist Year filter can use when
available from the provider/metadata — similar to the year vs.
original_year distinction used by beets/MusicBrainz Picard.

### Alternatives considered

None that I know of within MA itself — happy to hear if there's already a
workaround.
posts.title: Smart Playlist "Year" filter: use original recording year, not reissue/compilation year

**Problem**

Music Assistant never expires player registrations. When a client device re-registers under a new id — app reinstall with an install-scoped id, factory reset, restored-from-backup, a client identity bug — the old entry stays in Settings → Players as "unavailable" forever. There is no TTL, no auto-hide, and no bulk cleanup: each orphan must be found and deleted one at a time.

We maintain Sendspin clients (an Android TV / Apple TV visualizer player, plus contributions to SendspinKit — e.g. Sendspin/SendspinKit#36), and a single client-side identity bug on one Apple TV produced **seven** orphaned "unavailable" copies of the same physical device on one server before anyone noticed. Cleaning that server took the player list from 66 to 48 entries, all removed one by one. We've since made our client ids reinstall-stable, but no client can prevent this class of cruft in general — factory resets alone guarantee a slow drip of orphans for every user, and every player provider (not just Sendspin) is affected.

**Proposal**

1. **Auto-hide unavailable players after N days** (configurable, e.g. default 30; off = current behavior). Hidden, not deleted — a hidden player that reconne
posts.title: Stale-player hygiene: auto-hide long-unavailable players + bulk 'remove unavailable' action

There's currently no easy way to share what you're listening to with another MA user. Exporting a playlist as a file works, but it's not the same as a simple "hey, check out this track" moment — it requires extra steps and the recipient still has to manually import it.

## Proposed solution
A Share button in the player (and in context menus for tracks, artists and playlists) that generates a shareable link. When someone opens the link in their own MA instance, it resolves the item against their available providers automatically — regardless of which providers they use.

The key insight: user A on Spotify and user B on Apple Music can both open the same link and find the right track, because the link uses provider-agnostic identifiers (like ISRC or MusicBrainz ID) and falls back to a simple search if needed.

## Use cases
* Share a "now playing" status in chats or on social media
* Send a track or playlist recommendation to a friend who also uses MA

## Technical note
This would work similarly to the "My Home Assistant" button — a stateless redirect link where all the item info is encoded in the URL itself. No central database or storage needed.

As a side
posts.title: Share track/artist/playlist across MA instances via a shareable link

posts.excerpt:
I'd like to propose an API for pre-caching of music/podcasts for offline play. Current Sendspin requires a consistent and not too segmented internet connection between client and server, so it's hardly usable for spotty connections on roads and trains.

The idea is that offline-capable apps pre-cache these files to app-private storage, so it's explicitly _not_ meant to start a second music library for other apps or users to access. Rather, the cache would be used only by that app for offline play on planes, or to bridge timespans without internet, and for limited search to find such cached tracks. Apps would be aware of the canonical storage location on the server, so any metadata (playback history, listening position, favorites etc.) would still be persisted and visible to other clients, including pure Sendspin clients.

Clients of the proposed API would not necessarly get the original data. Rather, they receive a version targetted at their playback abilities, also taking into account reduced bandwidth. So the audio might be transcoded to a different codec, bit rate and/or bit depth. Volume-adjustments and other DSP workload might already be applied.

posts.excerpt:
Currently, as described in a comment [here](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5849#issuecomment-4966505097), Music Assistant disallows setting higher buffer sizes on machines at certain RAM thresholds.

This is an opinionated position, but disallowing a feature on an arbitrary threshold is removing some of the freedoms of the software user who may know the compromises made in order for it to work. Before this option was removed, I had run a perfectly stable server on a setting that is now no longer available to me (and the experience is now worse because of it).

I suggest that instead of removing the option from the frontend entirely, that the other buffer sizes are offered, and a user provided an appropriate warning that it may cause stability or OOM issues in some situations, if the hardware is below certain memory thresholds.

Additionally, I suspect that these thresholds have been set too high. I outline some thoughts about this [in this follow up comment](https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5849#issuecomment-4966603603) on the same original issue.
posts.title: Allow higher buffer sizes on lower memory devices

### What happened?

Browsing the "Metal" genre shows a huge amount of music that isn't metal at all — mainstream rock, pop-rock, etc. mixed in with genuine metal albums. Traced the cause to `music_assistant/helpers/resources/genres/genre_mapping.json`: the top-level `metal` genre's `aliases` list includes `"Rock"`, `"Hard Rock"`, and `"Rock / Indie"` — all of which are also present in (or clearly belong to) the separate top-level `rock` genre.

Because `"Rock"` is a generic tag used across huge swaths of non-metal music (way more file libraries tag things simply `Rock` than tag them with an actual metal subgenre), this single alias entry ends up dumping a large share of a user's entire rock collection int
posts.title: Genre mapping: 'Rock' incorrectly aliased into 'Metal', polluting the Metal genre with non-metal music

posts.excerpt:
Summary

On a 4-core Intel N100 mini PC (Music Assistant 2.9, filesystem_local provider, 65,387 candidate tracks), the Sonic Analysis background scan projects 317–635 days to cover the full library (measured, not estimated — see below). For comparison, Plex's own Sonic Analysis feature completed a comparable-sized library on the same physical host in 2 weeks. That gap (roughly 10-20x) is far larger than I'd expect from "different implementation," so I dug into why.

I don't think this is a single bug — it looks like three separate, compounding design choices, all deliberate (I found a maintainer comment in #5686 confirming the CPU-only, "polite background citizen" philosophy), but I think the combination is worth reconsidering for hosts with low core counts, where the current formula lands in the worst-case bucket.

Measured baseline

- Host: 4-core Intel N100, background_scan_concurrency=2 (default for ≥4 cores)
- Run window: 489.37s (8m 9s), cancelled mid-run for measurement purposes
- Results: 21,472 tracks completed Loudness Analysis in that window (~43.9 tracks/sec), but only 7 tracks completed the full pipeline including Sonic Analysis (~1 track per ~70s aggregate a
posts.title: Sonic Analysis background scan is ~10-20x slower than expected on small hosts — single-threaded inference, no batching, float32-only

I believe we can take some inspiration from what Meelo is doing with its Artist page: https://github.com/Arthi-chaud/Meelo/blob/main/docs/screenshots/web/artist-page-full.png

- `Toggle view mode list/thumb`, `Sort options` and `collapse/expand this listing` are currently per artist. It would make sense for those settings to be remembered and applied globally instead, so that we can default to `Thumbs view`, for example.
- Sections are currently displayed in a fixed order: Albums, Tracks, Top Tracks, Similar Artists, etc. There could be an edit mode, like the one for the Home page, that would allow us to choose the order and visibility for each section, applied globally.
- We can already **filter** releases per type, but it would make sense to **separate** them per type instead. Inside a "Releases" section, we would have subsections for "Albums", "Singles", "EP", etc. There should be a `Separate releases per type` toggle, assuming some users would prefer to keep all releases together.
- In `Thumbs view`, under each album, we currently repeat the album artist's name, which is already displayed at the top of the page. Unless a release has multiple album artists, we should drop t

Volume normalization works well now when album level replay gain information is provided, but it still causes problems for albums without like when replay gain information isn't in tags or playing from streaming providers (like Tidal) in my experience. For instance, listening to [White Halo by Heaven in Her Arms](https://musicbrainz.org/release-group/cdd4091a-7cd9-4285-9cb3-473039227988) I get a massive jump from +0.8dB to -10.3dB between the first and second track. This is after initial playback, obviously.

I'd love to see volume normalization [like Roon's](https://help.roonlabs.com/portal/en/kb/articles/volume-leveling#Volume_Leveling_Modes) that allows for album level adjustments rather than track level. Their "Auto" setting that "track adjustments when playing adjacent tracks from different albums, and album level adjustments when playing adjacent tracks from the same album" basically meant I didn't need to care about adding ReplayGain tags to my library (which you fairly say is a bit of a crutch). 

A potentially leaner solution that I think would really help would be to be able to add a setting that disables volume normalization for album playback - don't add normalizati

posts.excerpt:
Hi everyone,

I would like to propose a small but significant improvement regarding the frontend localization when Music Assistant runs as a Home Assistant app.

Currently, when the Home Assistant system language is set to Serbian Latin (`sr-Latn`) and Music Assistant is set to "Auto (follow system configuration)", MA opens in Serbian Cyrillic (`sr`). While explicitly selecting Serbian Latin in MA fixes the main interface, the initial 'Authenticating...' dialog still defaults to Cyrillic.

When discussing this, it was pointed out that Music Assistant is not exclusively a Home Assistant app. I completely agree, but given that Music Assistant is a proud part of the Open Home Foundation, there should at least be strict interoperability regarding system configuration and language matching between ecosystem apps.

Could we implement a check so that when Music Assistant detects it is running inside the HA ecosystem, it accurately inherits the host's specific language variant (like distinguishing between `sr-Latn` and `sr`) instead of falling back to a general default?

Thank you for considering this and for all your great work on Music Assistant!
posts.title: [Feature Request] Automatically detect and use Home Assistant language context (Open Home Interoperability)

## MEDIUM · Provider/core config secrets readable by any authenticated user (missing role gate)

### Summary
`config/providers/get_value` and `config/core/get_value` are registered as API commands with **no `required_role`**, so any authenticated user — including a non-admin / guest role — can read raw config values, including `SECURE_STRING` secrets (streaming-service credentials, SSL private-key material, etc.). ## HIGH · Reflected XSS in the OAuth callback page → session-token theft / account takeover

**CWE-79 / CWE-116.**

### Summary
`WebserverController._handle_auth_callback` builds the OAuth "Login Successful" page by string-replacing placeholders into `helpers/resources/oauth_callback.html` without any HTML/JS escaping. The replaced `{REDIRECT_URL}` value is attacker-influenceable (derived from the OAuth `return_url`) and lands inside a `<script>` string literal, so a single quote breaks out of the string and executes arbitrary JavaScript in the Music Assistant web origin — with the victim's freshly-minted auth token in scope.

### Location (line numbers as of `dev` @ `b86539f`)
- Sink: `music_assistant/controllers/webserver/controller.py:968-971`
  ```python
  success_html = success_html.replace("{TOKEN}", token)
  success_html = success_html.replace("{REDIRECT_URL}", final_redirect_url)

> **Status: already fixed.** Resolved by music-assistant/server#4544 (merged 2026-07-02), which removes the legacy `/imageproxy?provider=&path=` query-string form and its `_is_safe_imageproxy_request_path` validator. Filed here for the public record per maintainer request to split the coordinated private report (`GHSA-5cv4-xxvj-mpvc`) into one item per finding. No further action needed beyond confirming the fix reaches a release.

## Summary — unauthenticated arbitrary image-file read via legacy `/imageproxy` (CWE-22 / CWE-23)

The deprecated `/imageproxy?provider=&path=&size=&fmt=` route was registered on the **unauthenticated** stream server. Its safety check accepted empty-scheme (local) paths and performed no absolute-path or containment validation, so a remote, unauthenticated attacker could read arbitrary image-extension files anywhere on the host filesystem — and extract embedded cover-art from arbitrary media files.

## Impact

```
GET http://<host>:<stream-port>/imageproxy?provider=builtin&path=/absolute/path/to/file.png
```

returned the file bytes with **no authentication**. Scope was constrained (not unrestricted `/etc/passwd` read), which is why it was rated HIGH rathe

posts.excerpt:
## Environment

- **Home Assistant integration**: Music Assistant HA integration
- **Trigger**: `music_assistant.play_media` called simultaneously from two parallel Home Assistant script instances targeting two different `media_player` entities

## Description

When a Home Assistant automation calls a script in parallel for two kids' bedroom speakers, one or both speakers randomly stop playing in the middle of a track. The issue is intermittent — it does not happen every time, which makes it hard to reproduce deterministically.

This has been confirmed to occur with both **local library tracks** (`library://track/XX`) and **Spotify tracks/playlists**.

The same speakers work perfectly with a separate bedtime automation that uses an identical parallel structure calling `music_assistant.play_media` on both speakers. That automation has never exhibited this issue.

## Broken: Wake-up automation + script

**Automation** (mode: `single`):
```yaml
triggers:
  - trigger: time
    at: sensor.bedroom_speaker_turn_off_time

actions:
  - action: input_boolean.turn_off
    target:
      entity_id: input_boolean.kids_bedtime

  - parallel:
      - alias: kid_1
        action: script.wake_up_kid

Hey all 👋

I wanted to share a Home Assistant add-on I've been running alongside Music Assistant: **Metadata Remote** — a web-based audio tag editor that opens right inside the HA sidebar via ingress.

**Why it pairs well with MA:** MA leans heavily on good metadata — artist/album grouping, genres, artwork, etc. When I hit files with wrong or missing tags, I wanted to fix them *without* pulling files off my NAS, opening Picard/Mp3tag on a desktop. This lets me edit tags in-place, on the same share MA already uses, straight from the HA UI on any device.

It's a packaging of the excellent [metadata-remote](https://github.com/wow-signal-dev/metadata-remote) by @wow-signal-dev (AGPL-3.0) — all credit for the editor itself goes there. My add-on wraps it for Home Assistant and adds:

- **CIFS/SMB mounting** at runtime — point it at your NAS share (the same one MA uses), or fall back to the HA `/media` folder.
- **Ingress** — runs inside the HA frontend, no extra port or separate login.

**What the editor itself does:**
- Edit standard + fully custom tags.
- **Bulk apply** any field (or album art) to a whole folder in one click.
- **Album art** upload/preview/delete + auto-r

posts.excerpt:
Hi Team,

First of all, thank you for this amazing project! 

I would like to propose a clean, architectural solution for a persistent issue in the Media Browser (Browse view): the default sorting order.

## The Problem
Currently, when browsing local file-based systems (e.g., Local files, SMB shares), the default sort order is set to 'Original'. On Linux filesystems, 'Original' means the items are listed based on inodes/filesystem indexes, resulting in a completely scrambled, unreadable order. 

While users can manually switch the sort order to 'Alphabetical' on the UI, this setting is not persistent. Upon page refresh, pagination (loading more chunks), or navigating deeper into folders, the frontend reverts back to 'Original'. This makes browsing larger local directories highly frustrating.

### The Solution (Proposal)
Instead of trying to fix state persistence in the frontend or forcing a global default that might break streaming providers (like Spotify or Tidal, which rely on 'Original' to keep their curated order), **the default sort order should be handled at the Provider level.**

It would be amazing to have a dropdown setting within each Music Provider's config
posts.title: Provider-level default sort order for Media Browser

**Music Assistant version:** 2.9.3
**Provider:** Audiobookshelf (music provider)

### Symptom

The Audiobookshelf podcast sync (and the recommendations fetch) fail *wholesale* when a single podcast episode has an out-of-range year in its date:

```
WARNING (MainThread) [music_assistant.tasks] Background task Sync Audiobookshelf podcasts failed: year must be in 1..9999, not 10909
WARNING (MainThread) [music_assistant.music] Error while fetching recommendations from Audiobookshelf: year must be in 1..9999, not 40300
```

### Cause

An Audiobookshelf podcast had episodes whose date parsed to an out-of-range year (e.g. `10909`, `40300`). MA raises a `ValueError` building the `date`/`datetime`, and the exception propagates up and aborts the entire **Sync Audiobookshelf podcasts** background task (and the recommendations fetch). As a result **none** of the provider's podcasts/audiobooks import — not just the offending episode.

### Expected

An episode with an invalid / out-of-range date should still be **imported and shown — just with an empty / unset date** — and the sync should continue. A bad date value should degrade to "no date"; it should never skip the episode, and never abort th

posts.excerpt:
While it's usually desirable for both speakers in a stereo pair to have the same volume level, sometimes there are a specific situations where it's desirable for one side to have more volume than the other.

For example:

- If one speaker has to be placed significantly further away from the listener, the soundstage won't be centred for them.
- Many active stereo speakers have all their amplification circuitry in one speaker, while the other is passive. The amplifier is calibrated for the length of cable expected between the two speakers, meaning a longer cable may make one speaker softer than the other.

Manual balance controls are a common feature in hi-fi systems and advanced OS volume settings.

Hopefully this feature can also be added to Music Assistant on a per-player basis.
posts.title: Left-right audio balance

posts.excerpt:
I noticed a UX gap that affects all `PLAYER_CONTROL_NATIVE` players (DLNA renderers, Sonos via S1, Squeezebox, etc.) but not `PLAYER_CONTROL_FAKE` players. Wanted to check intent before submitting a PR.

## Observation

In `PlayerController._handle_cmd_volume_set` ([controller.py](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/dev/music_assistant/controllers/players/controller.py)):

```python
if player.volume_control == PLAYER_CONTROL_NATIVE:
    await player.volume_set(device_volume)
    return    # no optimistic state update

if player.volume_control == PLAYER_CONTROL_FAKE:
    player.extra_data[ATTR_FAKE_VOLUME] = volume_level
    player.update_state()    # optimistic
```

For FAKE control MA optimistically updates state and pushes to clients. For NATIVE control it relies on the next poll cycle / event from the device. That delay is anywhere from a few ms (devices with proper LastChange events) to multiple seconds (JBL DLNA, for instance, does not emit RenderingControl events and depends entirely on the periodic poll).

Observable effect: dragging the volume slider in MA Web UI for a DLNA player makes the slider snap back to the prior value briefly before catching up. Fast mult
posts.title: Volume slider lag on PLAYER_CONTROL_NATIVE players: intentional asymmetry vs FAKE?

When listening to radio streams that provide artwork via the ICY `StreamUrl` field (e.g., album covers from radio station APIs), Music Assistant ignores this URL entirely. Instead, it always performs a MusicBrainz lookup to find artwork, which:

- Overrides the station-provided cover with a (sometimes different) MusicBrainz result
- Adds unnecessary API calls when the stream already provides the correct artwork
- Returns no artwork at all for talk radio programs, regional stations, or lesser-known tracks that MusicBrainz doesn't index

Many radio stations (Radio France, FIP, RMC, Catalunya Radio, etc.) expose high-quality, real-time artwork through their APIs. Tools like Node-RED or custom ICY proxies can inject this artwork into `StreamUrl`, but MA currently discards it.

Parse the `StreamUrl` field from ICY metadata in `_parse_icy_metadata()` and pass it to `_update_radio_stream_metadata()` as `image_url`.

posts.excerpt:
This is a request for:

- a text configuration mechanism for Music Assistant
- a commitment to configuration-as-code as a supported aspect of the project. 

# Background

A trial of music-assistant this week to replace a 12-player multizone audio system has led to one overriding conclusion:
**UI configuration is tedious and repetitive**.

By contrast our existing multizone system runs from [a single config.json](https://github.com/markferry/multizone-audio/blob/master/example.config.json).

# Options

## Generate `settings.json`
MA `settings.json` mixes static and dynamic data which makes it unsuitable for version-control.
It is representative of the current state, not a *configuration mechanism*.

There's potential to generate `settings.json` from separate `core.json`, `providers.json`, `players.json` files.

For this a **configuration schema** would be a prerequisite.

## CLI tool and MA API

A CLI tool that interacts with the MA API (some overlap with #5355, perhaps) could be used to orchestrate configuration changes.
posts.title: Configuration as Code

posts.excerpt:
**Feature Request**

Currently, the "Default enqueue option for Track item(s)" in 
Settings → System → Player Queues only offers two options:

- Play (and keep queue)
- Play (and replace queue)

**What's missing**

There is no way to set **"Play next (and keep queue)"** as the 
default action for tracks. This option exists in the track 
context menu, but it cannot be saved as a permanent default.

**Expected behavior**

The same enqueue options available in the context menu should 
also be available as default settings in Player Queue settings, 
specifically:

- Play next (and keep queue)
- Play next (and replace queue)
- Add to queue

**Why this is useful**

When listening to music and browsing for the next song, most 
users want to queue it up as "play next" rather than 
immediately interrupting playback or adding it to the very end 
of a long queue. Having to right-click every single time is 
cumbersome.
posts.title: Add "Play next (and keep queue)" as default enqueue option for Track items

1st thank you very much to all the folks working on this project! Fantastic!

2nd apologies of this is already in system or queue, I'm a noob here.

When listening to a music stream, playlist or even an album, you hear a track that you like and want to 'get back to it' and learn more about it and perhaps add it to library/playlist. On the MA frontend, mobile or desktop app in the 'currently playing' UI element would it be possible to have a 'button' to capture this track in some type of a list? posts.excerpt:
I find radio stations can have different volume levels and it made me think how great it would be if we had a 'Gain' setting for each Radio Station, so any particularly quiet or loud station, or just one you wanted to change a bit for any reason could be adjusted - at the source as it were.

Volume can of course be adjusted at the media player, but then possibly needs readjusting whenever stations are changed and under Home Assistant automations that would need special volume control built-in for every automation and any chosen station and if MA is used externally to HA, then that adjustment is lost.

The ideal solution would be if we could adjust the Gain for each Radio Station in MA itself so that follows through to whatever method is used to play that audio, whenever and wherever it is used.

A fairly trivial nicety, but I think it would be marvellous to have.
posts.title: Radio Station Gain

posts.excerpt:

### Feature Description

Add an optional **opt-in** setting to the Filesystem music providers that allows Music Assistant to write fetched artwork back to the local source (SMB, NFS, WebDAV or local disk), following the existing artwork file naming conventions:

- `artist.jpg` / `folder.jpg` — artist thumbnail in artist folder (with extra option to create artist folder when folder doesn't exicst (feat. artists for example).
- `fanart.jpg` — fan art / background banner
- `logo.png` — artist logo used in the Artist view
- `cover.jpg` / `folder.jpg` — coverart for Album in album folder (most propperly tagged music using Picard will already have these).

They could be set individually by checking a lightbox, so the user has full control over what they do and don't want to be written back to their storage.

This could also include an option to allow or disallow overwriting existing files (preventing overwriting of personal curated images and/or allowing for periodic updates for more recent fan art).

When MA fetches artist images from metadata providers (e.g. Fanart.tv, MusicBrainz), they currently only live in the MA internal database/cache. If an artist

posts.excerpt:
First, is there a current discussion regarding how the player queue functions?

If not, I would like to start one. I don't mean to complain at all. I am constantly amazed at the work that goes into HOAS and all the other addons by such an amazing community. But I also think community feedback helps make everything better.

I find the queue's functionality perhaps overthought and not very user-friendly. The first point is the existence of two separate sections of a queue, played/not played. The way these two 'sides' of the queue work together introduces quirks that a workaround just can't fix.

If there is a track that I would like to hear again, triggering "play next" on a track in the 'played' side of the queue rewinds the entire queue to play that track along with all the other tracks that had also already been played. 

It is also frustrating to use the 'move track' options, especially when you have a queue with many tracks. I should add that you cannot move a track from the 'played' side to the 'unplayed' side by using the 'move track' option.

### Summary

I'd like Music Assistant to automatically power smart speakers on when playback is requested, and power them off after a configurable idle period – using the existing **Player → Power Control** feature as the underlying mechanism.

---

### Proposed Behaviour

**Auto Power On**
When a player is powered off but still configured in MA, it should remain visible in the player list rather than disappearing. When playback to that player is requested, MA should:
1. Display a brief waiting indicator

3. Wait for the player to come back online and announce itself on the network

posts.excerpt:
# Music Assistant doesn't let you pick which copy plays

When you've got the same album from more than one source — a local rip plus Qobuz, say — Music Assistant merges them into one entry and quietly decides which copy to play. That happens on the server, so it's the same no matter how you're using it: web UI, the Home Assistant integration, or your own code against the API all get whatever MA picked. There's no "use this one instead" on the merged album, and nothing tells you which copy you got unless you go dig through the queue.

The thinking behind it is "it grabs the best quality, and they're the same album anyway." The second half is where it gets shaky, and it gets shaky in exactly the cases that are easy to miss: two copies that look identical in every way you can see, but don't sound the same.

## How the pick works

It's a score. For lossless files it's basically sample rate plus bit depth, so a CD-quality 16/44 file scores 60, a 24/96 scores 120, and a 24/192 scores 216. Lossy formats score way down around 1 or 2. On top of that there's a small bonus for local files (+2, plus another +1 if the item's in your library) and for other local servers like Plex (+1); s

### The problem

When using a Yamaha MusicCast receiver through Music Assistant with Sendspin/AirPlay as the preferred output protocol, advancing to the next track changes the parent MusicCast player's volume unexpectedly.

In this setup, the Music Assistant player `Living Room` is a Yamaha RX-V6A MusicCast player whose preferred output protocol is the Sendspin bridge for its AirPlay endpoint. On a normal `next` command, the Living Room volume dropped from 36% to 26% without any explicit volume command from Home Assistant or the user.

This looks like an AirPlay/Sendspin volume scale mismatch with the linked MusicCast parent:

- Music Assistant restarts the Sendspin/AirPlay bridge on track change.
- The bridge starts `cliraop` with `-volume 36`, copied from the parent MusicCast player's Music Assistant volume.
- The Yamaha AirPlay endpoint maps that to native MusicCast raw volume `43` out of `161`.
- Music Assistant's MusicCast provider reads that back as `int(43 / 161 * 100) == 26`.
- The parent player is then exposed as 26% volume.

UI integration inside the player controls
Support for voice assistants / Assist

Why This Would Be Useful

Many media platforms and audio systems already provide this feature because it is a very common use case.

posts.excerpt:
One of the design decision for the genre system shipped within MA is to use a predefined list of genres and aliases combined with some MusicBrainz metadata matching to fully "automate" genres definition and creation.

This is amazing for two particular use cases:

1. Users using MA as a "bridge" between various music streaming services / providers (where genres can be all over the place) 
2. Users that have a local library that is  messy, not "clean", not properly curated and tagged.

So basically, it solves the problem where the "Source" is messy genre-wise. All good in these scenarios 👍 

## The Problem

This approach will provide a really bad experience for a third type of user : **the Local Library Collector with carefully curated and manually tagged files.** 

This user already invested the work to clean it's library, tag the files the way he wants it, assign genres based on his understanding, his personal classification and sometimes his own regional definition for some musical areas that MusicBrainz can simply lack to differentiate.

For this third type of user I'm advocating here ... and let me explain the bad experience.

### The problem

The **SiriusXM** music provider produces constant audio dropouts (multi-second gaps, continuous). Spotify and other providers on the same MA instance and network play with zero dropouts.

> Scope note for triage: this issue is auto-labeled `spotify`, but it is a **SiriusXM provider** bug. Spotify is referenced only as the unaffected comparison/workaround. Please relabel to `siriusxm`.

The defect is in the pinned `sxm==0.2.8` dependency (upstream `AngellusMortis/sxm-client` — no commits since 2021-07-24, same as PyPI 0.2.8), which predates SiriusXM's move to Akamai token-auth. Session renewal *succeeds* (the SiriusXM API returns `200` with a fresh `SXMAKTOKEN`), but the Akamai edge keeps `403`-ing the next segment/playlist, producing an endless renew loop. A full sanitized debug trace and a suggested fix are in the issue comments below.

1. Add the SiriusXM provider with an All Access account (email login).
2. Play any SiriusXM channel to any player.
3. Audio streams cleanly for ~3 minutes after an add-on rest

posts.excerpt:
It is possible to create a Classical Music specific view but we are interested in how many MA users want this functionality so if you do then upvote this post!

Today, classical metadata gets squashed into the same flat "artists" list as everything else, there's no concept of a *Work* (the composition itself, separate from a particular recording), and you can't browse or search by composer. This proposal aims to fix that.

**Please tell us if you need something this proposal doesn't cover.** Easier to hear about it now than after we've shipped half of it.

## What metadata could we capture

For every track and album, where the source provides it: (These are the tags as supported by MusicBrainz)

posts.title: Sonos Provider wont play

posts.excerpt:
I'm running into a limitation with Home Assistant automations:

`music_assistant.get_queue` exposes queue/player metadata and current_item, but there is currently no reliable way to determine the originating playlist that populated the queue.

Observed behavior:

* `queue_id` remains stable even when switching playlists
* `current_item` only exposes track/radio metadata
* playlist provenance appears to be discarded once items are enqueued

Example use case:

* HA automations reacting differently depending on the currently active MA playlist
* Dashboard cards showing “Current Playlist”
* Toggling between two playlists - need to detect which playlist is currently playing

Would it be possible to expose one of:

* `current_playlist`
* `source_playlist`
* `queue_origin`
* or playlist metadata in `get_queue`

even if only when playback was initiated from a playlist URI?

Right now the only workaround is manually storing playlist names in helper entities when playback is started through HA automations.

posts.excerpt:
Currently, Music Assistant matches tracks [like so](https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/543):

> prefer MusicBrainz ID match or ISRC match
Album must exactly match
Title must exactly match
Version must exactly match
Fallback to duration match if both tracks have compilation (multi artist) albums

I'm currently using Navidrome to host my music collection so the "MusicBrainz ID" is provided through the OpenSubSonic API as `musicBrainzId` which is populated by the MusicBrainz Recording ID ([written to FLAC files as `MUSICBRAINZ_TRACKID` by Picard](https://picard-docs.musicbrainz.org/en/latest/appendices/tag_mapping.html#id39)). 

This mostly works out well, but problems come up when a collection contains two versions of the same album (OpenSubSonic returns a `version` to Music Assistant through the API). For example, imagine I had an [original 80s vinyl rip of Disintegration](https://musicbrainz.org/release/11af85e2-c272-4c59-a902-47f75141dc97) as well as a [CD rip of the remaster](https://musicbrainz.org/release/91fa2331-d8b4-4d1f-aa4d-53b1c54853e5) in my collection - the tracks on both these versions will have matching recording IDs so they will be matched,

posts.title: Propagated genres get imported with lower cases only

posts.excerpt:
The current logic of the (new) genre feature for local files is as follows
1. local nfo file
2. online sources such as MusicBrainz
3. propagated genre from tracks, if turned on in the "Local Files" provider

I personally do have my own genre matching and all my tracks therefore do have "my genres". I do not have local nfo files.

What happens is that if MusicBrainz can identify the artist properly, it will pull the genre (along with the bio and other metadata) from music brainz and I "dont want" MB's genre allocation.
I'm suggesting to change the logic to:
1. local nfo file
2. propagated genre from tracks, if turned on in the "Local Files" provider
3. online sources such as MusicBrainz
This would allow that you still get the bio and other items from the online metadata providers, but the genre would be propagated from the (local) tracks.

As a bonus (or alternative solution of the above), I was thinking if it would be a nice feature that you can turn on/off toggles if you actually even want the fields to be pulled from the online sources. In my specific use case,

I've got trouble bringing back some tracks from pause. Especially on Squeezelite.

There seem to be some conditions when I'm un-pausing tracks and they get stuck like this, and I think this problem with position numbers is causing it. Nudging to next track un-sticks the player, but it has been bugging me enough to make this post.

posts.excerpt:
## The problem

Music Assistant registers **four parallel player bridges** for a single physical Sonos speaker (a Sonos Beam in my case) that supports multiple protocols. All four are `enabled: true` in `settings.json` out of the box, despite the [Sonos player-support docs](https://www.music-assistant.io/player-support/sonos/) implying that AirPlay/DLNA variants for Sonos devices should be deduplicated.

The four concurrent bridges — each independently subscribing, probing, and keeping sessions alive — put the Sonos Beam into a sensitized state where routine network events (UPnP event subscriptions from HA, SSDP M-SEARCH responses, etc.) cascade to a media-pipeline refresh. On a Beam operating as a TV soundbar via HDMI-ARC/eARC, the media-pipeline refresh manifests as a brief ARC disconnect → TV (LG OLED in my case) retriggers its Dolby Vision handshake → "Resume playback" banner.

Ungraceful shutdown of MASS (`docker stop`) leaves residual subscription/session state on the Beam that **continues to cause the same drops at a lower frequency for many hours or until the device is factory-reset.** Factory-resetting the Beam dropped my TV-disruption rate from "every 4 minutes" to "every

posts.excerpt:
Description:
I am requesting a way to trigger Music Assistant’s internal "Source" routing—specifically for Plugin Providers like the VBAN Receiver—via Home Assistant automations.
The Problem:
Currently, there is a functional gap between the Music Assistant (MA) UI and Home Assistant (HA) actions. In the MA UI, I can manually switch a player (like a Sendspin/Squeezelite instance) to a VBAN stream. However, this cannot be automated in HA.
As clarified by developers, media_player.select_source in HA is designed for hardware-native inputs (HDMI, Line-in). Because many MA players are software-based, they report that they don’t support select_source, causing automations to fail even though the MA UI shows a "Source" picker for internal routing.
Proposed Solution:
Instead of trying to force this into the standard media_player.select_source (which creates ambiguity between hardware and software sources), I propose:

    A Dedicated MA Action: Create a specific Home Assistant action (e.g., music_assistant.select_routing_source) that allows us to programmatically switch a player to an MA-level source like VBAN, AirCast, or the MA Queue.

Hi,

I’d like to request support for the YouLyPlus lyrics provider (https://github.com/ibratabian17/YouLyPlus), or any other similar project, particularly its word-by-word synchronized lyrics feature.


YouLyPlus uses this as its backend
> [https://github.com/ibratabian17/lyricsplus](https://github.com/ibratabian17/lyricsplus)


I looked into the lyricsplus backend that YouLyPlus uses. The main server is:

Base URL: https://lyricsplus.prjktla.my.id
Endpoint: /v2/lyrics/get

Required parameters:
- title - song title
- artist - artist name
Optional parameters:
- album - album name
- duration - song duration in seconds
- isrc - ISRC code
- source - source preference order
- forceReload - bypass cache

Example request:
`curl "https://lyricsplus.prjktla.my.id/v2/lyrics/get?title=Never+gonna+give+you+up&artist=Rick+Astley"`

Backup mirrors:
- https://lyricsplus.atomix.one/
- https://lyricsplus.binimum.org
- https://lyricsplus.prjktla.workers.dev
- https://lyricsplus-seven.vercel.app

The API returns word-by-word synced lyrics (type: "WORD") when available, or line-synced (type: "LINE").

### What version of Music Assistant is affected?

2.7.x (latest)

### What is the issue?

The LinkPlay/WiiM player provider does not passively reflect playback originated outside Music Assistant. When a user starts audio from the WiiM app (Pandora, Spotify Connect to the WiiM, AirPlay to the WiiM, Tidal Connect, line-in, etc.), the MA player for that device stays in `off` / idle state even though the device is actively playing audio.

### Why this is a request, not a bug

Per @MarvinSchenkel in #4621 (closed `NOT_PLANNED`):

> This is expected behaviour in Music Assistant. You are right that this does not happen with Airplay, but that is simply because it has not been built yet. MA should mark a speaker as 'active' whenever audio is playing.

So passive reflection is the intended design across providers. The DLNA provider implements it. AirPlay and Squeezelite were noted as not-yet-implemented at the time of #4621. This request is to add the same behavior to the **LinkPlay/WiiM** provider, so behavior is consistent across all player types.

- Device: WiiM Amp Ultra, firmware Linkplay.5.2.809633

posts.excerpt:
**The short story:**
It is possible that Sendspin does not work with some Chromecast devices. There is nothing we can do about this. In a future update of MA, we will automatically detect this and disable the protocol on the device.

**The long story**
To make Sendspin work with Chromecast based devices, we rely on the (bloated) implementation of the Cast protocol, which is browser based. We basically run a browser version of Sendspin inside the on-device browser of the Chromecast device. Newer devices implement the 'Google Cast for Audio (GC4A) 2.0', which is a lightweight (read non bloated) implementation that simply just does not implement the audio API's we require to run Sendspin.

This is a (non-exhaustive) list of devices that currently implement GC4A 2.0. These devices will most likely not work with Sendspin. Google aims to release this new version of Cast to more existing devices, so this list will likely grow in the future:
- Bose: Wifi Speaker and Smart Soundbars
- JBL: Charge 5 Wi-Fi / Boombox 3 Wi-Fi / Authentics 200, 300, and 500
- Samsung: Music Frame / Soundbars
- LG: Soundbars S90TY/SG10TY/SE70Q/S80Q/S90Q
- Bang & Olufsen Beosound 2 / Beocore Connect
- Sonoro Maest

First of all, when viewing the list of Albums, it would be good to have an 'Artist/Album' sort option, so sorted first by Sort Album Artist tag and then by the Sort Album Tag. This is a very useful sort order and was introduced as a special option in iTunes many years ago. All the other sort options are perfectly valid and provide powerful sorting options for those who need them, but MA is seriously missing that 'by Artist by Album' sort option when trying to view a long list of Albums.

## Description

When playback stops (end of queue or pause) and resumes later, the Sendspin AirPlay bridge shows as "connected" and "playing" in Music Assistant but no audio data is actually transmitted to the AirPlay receiver. The MA client appears to be working but is silently failing to send data.

## Environment

- Music Assistant v2.8.2 (HA add-on)
- Home Assistant Supervised on Raspberry Pi 5 (Bookworm 64-bit)
- AirPlay receiver: shairport-sync (managed by Snapcast via `airplay://` source)
- Sendspin server on port 8927
- Players in All Rooms group: Google Nest Mini (Cast), Apple TV (AirPlay), CerberusAirPlay (AirPlay/Snapcast tap)

1. Play music via Spotify Connect -> MA -> All Rooms group (Cast + AirPlay players)
2. Let playback end naturally (end of queue) or pause for extended period (overnight)
3. Resume playback or start new queue
4. Nest (Cast) and Apple TV resume normally
5. CerberusAirPlay (AirPlay via Sendspin) shows "playing" in MA but receives no audio data

posts.excerpt:
**Feature Request:** 
Shuffle should optionally operate as a per-session or per-queue setting rather than always being a persistent player-level state that survives across separate playback sessions.

**Currently**
When shuffle is enabled on a Music Assistant player — whether via the UI or via media_player.shuffle_set in a HA automation — it is set persistently on that player. It remains enabled regardless of what is played next, even if the queue is fully replaced via enqueue: replace. This means:
	∙	Enable shuffle for a morning playlist automation at 5:45 AM
	∙	Hours later, open MA and play Abbey Road with “replace queue”
	∙	Abbey Road plays in shuffled order, not track sequence

The shuffle state carries over even though the intent was clearly a fresh, unrelated playback session.

**My Feelings/Request**
Shuffle feels fundamentally different from other persistent player settings like volume or repeat. Volume persisting makes intuitive sense — you expect your speaker to remember how loud it was. But shuffle is tied to what you’re playing and why, not to the speaker itself. I would suspect most users expect shuffle to be a property of a playback session, not a permanen

**Summary**
It would be great if the Party Plugin exposed the guest access QR code as a Home Assistant `image` entity, so it can be displayed on any Lovelace dashboard without opening the Music Assistant UI directly.

**Use case**
I run a Fire HD 10 tablet (2019, KFMAWI) as a wall-mounted dashboard using Fully Kiosk Browser. The tablet's Amazon WebView is stuck at version 90 and cannot be updated — this means the Music Assistant frontend (`/#/party`) renders as a blank white page. There is no way to root this device or replace the WebView.

A HA image entity containing the QR code would allow me (and others in similar situations) to display the guest join code directly on a Lovelace dashboard without ever needing to load the MA frontend.

The older [HAMusicAssistantJukebox](https://github.com/DJS91/HAMusicAssistantJukebox) custom integration already provides `music_assistant_jukebox_internal_qr_code` and `music_assistant_jukebox_external_qr_code` as image entities — proof that this is both useful and technically feasible. It's very easy to accidentally set the volume much higher or lower than intended when trying to make a small adjustment.

The only workaround right now is leaving the native Music Assistant UI and using custom Home Assistant cards (like Mushroom Media Player with `volume_buttons` enabled) on a Lovelace dashboard. ## Problem

When an external source (Spotify Connect, AirPlay, AriaCast) tries to start playback on a player that is currently a member of a sync group, `select_source` raises `PlayerCommandFailed("Player X is currently grouped")`. However, all three plugin providers call `select_source` via `mass.create_task()` (fire-and-forget), so the exception is swallowed. The user has no indication that the player is grouped or that they need to take manual action.

2. Create a Spotify Connect instance targeting player A
3. Start Spotify playback targeting player A

posts.title: Sync Group Players - no longer support volume control through Home Assistant

posts.excerpt:
## Summary

`SyncGroupPlayer` is a virtual abstraction representing a sync group as a single entity for UI, volume control, and plugin interaction. However, throughout the codebase, it is **not** treated interchangeably with physical players. Instead, numerous call sites contain special-case logic that checks player type, player ID prefix, or `sync_leader` attributes to bridge the gap between the physical and logical layers.

This creates a recurring pattern where every new feature that interacts with players must independently discover and work around the fact that sync groups are a different beast -- leading to subtle bugs (see [PR music-assistant/server#3512](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/pull/3512) for a concrete example with plugin volume callbacks).

**Goal:** At all but the lowest-level physical transport/plugin layer, a `SyncGroupPlayer` should be 100% interchangeable with an individual physical player. Most providers and controllers should not need to know or care whether they are operating on a sync group or an individual player.

posts.title: Onn Large Wi-Fi Speaker will not sync playback with an Apple TV

posts.excerpt:
Music-assistant (MA) players relies on players being on auto-discovered on the same subnet/VLAN, which creates a conflict when installed as an addon for HA. 

Using an isolated subnet/VLAN for wifi-enabled smart devices is quite commonly recommended security practice. For a lot of home-assistant (HA) addons it is required to have HA on the same subnet as said devices. Shelly, ESPHome etc but also the products that are cloud connected and a black box on your network.

Multimedia devices are a middle-of-the-road thing where you sort of have to trust them on your regular network if you want to be able to easily connect and cast to them, possibly restricted by some firewall rules if you are ambitious with security. 

So the current solution is to use the HA Mediaplayer provider with HA as a proxy to the device. It works... ish. But as the MA documentation for Home Assistant Media Players states multiple times, it is very much not recommended, and using a native player in MA is preferred.

In conclusion, it would make sense for MA to allow for manual configuration of players alongside with the auto discovery feature.

## Description

After upgrading to Music Assistant 2.8.x (currently on 2.8.1), the **Output Channel Mode** setting (Left / Right / Stereo / Mono) is no longer visible in the player settings for AirPlay 2 players.

These settings are needed to configure stereo pairs (e.g., two speakers set to Left and Right channels respectively).

- **Installation:** Docker (`ghcr.io/music-assistant/server:latest`), standalone (not HA add-on)

- **Host:** Raspberry Pi

## Steps to reproduce

1. Open Music Assistant UI → Settings → Players
2. Click on an AirPlay 2 player
3. Look for "Output Channel Mode" setting — not present

## Expected behavior

- The Output Channel Mode setting should be available in AirPlay player settings, as documented at https://www.music-assistant.io/player-support/airplay/

## Additional context

- The [AirPlay documentation](https://www.music-assistant.io/player-support/airplay/) still references Output Channel Mode under "Advanced Protocol Settings"

posts.title: Web player disappears when in Party mode

posts.excerpt:
I have 2 older uPNP players which don't allow you to Pause live streams - they just ignore the Pause command when the source is a stream.  This means MA thinks it's paused the music and is in "paused" state, but the music is still playing.  In the Lyrion Music Server (aka Squeezebox) uPNP Bridge plugin this is solved by providing an option to replace Pause with Stop if the source is a stream.  The description is 


```
<live_pause>0 | 1</live_pause > default = 1

Some players will not pause when playing live streams (e.g.webradio). It’s correct that although you can buffer or “timeshift” livestream, in most case it does not make sense as gap with real time increases forever, at every pause. For such players, the bridge can commute LMS’ pause request into a stop (only when playing a livestream)
```


I wondered if it would be possible to add a similar option to the uPNP provider

posts.title: TuneIn provider (triplej stream) intermittently stopping playback

posts.excerpt:
### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.8.0

### The problem

I was delighted to see a new release of MA this afternoon. However, I was not so happy to see that, despite 2.8.0 being numbered  a minor release under [SemVer](https://semver.org/#spec-item-7), there was a big warning at the top of the release notes (I'm glad I glanced at them!) saying that this release does, in fact, include breaking changes. This undermines the purpose of using SemVer, in my opinion—I believe that *any* breaking change should increment the major counter so that users can more effectively gauge the amount of research they should do before upgrading. Contrary to how some projects operate, a "major release" shouldn't have to mean major changes were made—simply breaking changes. Check out Tom Preston-Werner's ["Major Version Numbers are Not Sacred"](https://tom.preston-werner.com/2022/05/23/major-version-numbers-are-not-sacred) for a much more qualified argument about why breaking changes should always be major releases. Thanks!

When using the Nugs.net music provider, any action that calls \`get_track\` fails with a \`NotImplementedError\`. This affects:

\`\`\`

When Radio Browser has been added as a provider and looking at their list of stations, by Tag or by Country etc, it seems there's no way to control the sort order of the displayed list.

The 'Sort' icon and drop down menu is at the top as usual, but it does not work correctly. It defaults to 'Original' and if you choose 'Alphabetically' or 'Alphabetically descending' the order does change, but not to what has been selected and the drop down menu still shows 'Original' is selected.

Very easy to see the order is not 'Alphabetically' when that is selected as names starting with a number are mixed up with regular alpha names and the entire list seems to be some random jumble and not 'Alphabetically' at all.

Since elsewhere this list order control menu seems to work as it should and the menu does reflect what was selected, I think this is simply a glitch limited to the Radio Browser list display.

Not a huge deal, but makes trying to find items in a long list rather hard so thought I should mention it.

posts.excerpt:
I did mention it in another thread but thought it worth its own FR.

The Rayo app is Bauer Media's own radio station aggregator, for all the radio stations owned by Bauer here in the UK and that comprises many of the main radio stations, which are not otherwise accessible through direct URLs as they include an ID number that Bauer change on a regular basis, just to prevent listening, apart from through their Rayo app.

Much as I hate that practice, it seems to me that if MA added Rayo as a provider, much like BBC Sounds, it would immediately make a lot of major UK stations available to MA users, so I'd like to propose this as a Feature Request, to add Rayo as a provider.

posts.excerpt:
I have mentioned this in the Q&A sections but perhaps it should be here.

MA is currently unable to play radio station URLs like:-

`http://www.radiofeeds.net/playlists/bauerflash.pls?station=absoluteclassicrockhigh-aac`

These are required to circumvent the station owners frequently obfuscating the actual URL to prevent it being used to listen to the station. Daft if you ask me, but I'd like to request that MA be updated to be able to play URLs like the above so we can use MA to play these stations.

Having said that, the stations that have this problem are all available on the Rayo app. If that could be added as a Provider, same as BBC Sounds so we can just add the stations from there, then perhaps that's something to also be considered as well, or instead.

posts.excerpt:
## Problem

When a Sendspin bridge client reconnects (e.g. after a version upgrade or hostname change), the player's `device_info` (model/product_name, manufacturer, software_version) is not updated in Music Assistant — MA continues showing the old values.

## Root Cause

In `music_assistant/providers/sendspin/provider.py` ([source](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blob/main/music_assistant/providers/sendspin/provider.py)), `_handle_client_added()` calls `self.mass.players.register(player)` which raises `AlreadyRegisteredError` if the player is already registered. There is also an early check:

```python
if self.mass.players.get_player(client_id) is not None:
    self.logger.debug("Client %s already registered, skipping duplicate add event", client_id)
    return
```

When a bridge restarts, the sendspin client reconnects before MA processes `ClientRemovedEvent` (TCP keepalive timeout is slower than reconnect). The old player is still registered → new `SendspinPlayer` with fresh `DeviceInfo` is skipped entirely.

## Suggested Fix

posts.excerpt:
Hello, I recently was trying to make a ESP32 based small screen to show the album artwork playing on the music assistant.
In the debug log, I noticed one thing.

I used a homeassistant text_sensor to obtain the entity_picture attribute from home assistant. When I switch from a playing track to another. I first get an URL and in a few milliseconds get another one.
The first URL is pointing to the last artwork url, and second is the one to new url. Furthermore, they are in different string combinations.
I looked in MA log. I guess I found the reason.
The first URL is generated by metadata.py including provider+image_format+size=500+path. And the second URL is generated by images.py including path+provider+size=0.

In my use case I need to ignore the first one and only download the picture from the second url which is for the new track.

I would like to ask if this is intended, and I was thinking to skip the first one by searching for "fmt=" string or "size=500" string, because new url doesn't contains that. I hope this will be not be changed in future and cause my code issue :)

posts.excerpt:
## Summary

Add an Overcast podcast provider that imports subscriptions and played status from [Overcast](https://overcast.fm), the popular iOS podcast app by Marco Arment.

Overcast exposes user data through an authenticated extended OPML export that includes podcast subscriptions (with RSS feed URLs) and per-episode played/progress state. This is enough to build a read-only podcast provider that auto-discovers a user's subscriptions and imports their listening history.

## Why Overcast?

- One of the most popular podcast apps on iOS
- Already exposes structured data: the extended OPML export at `/account/export_opml/extended` includes RSS feed URLs, episode GUIDs, played status, and progress timestamps
- Users migrating to Music Assistant for home audio want their existing podcast library to follow them without manually re-adding each show
- The existing `podcastfeed` provider handles single feeds well, but Overcast users often have 20-50+ subscriptions — a provider that bulk-imports from their account would close that gap

## Proposed Implementation

### Authentication
- Email/password login via `POST https://overcast.fm/login` (session cookie auth)
- No official API exists, so

posts.title: NumPy was built with baseline optimizations, but your machine doesn't support

posts.excerpt:
Hey everyone,
I (and probably many others) run home assistant virtualized in Proxmox. The default processor type (kvm64) does not support the new numpy version, which leads to music assistant not starting without a clear error (just a cryptic `NumPy was built with baseline optimizations:  (X86_V2) but your machine doesn't support: (X86_V2)`, see https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5005).
This can be very easily fixed by changing the CPU type of the VM, and I feel like it could be a time-saver for many people to include a short note like this in the update notes, if possible:

> [!WARNING]
> This update introduces a dependency update, which renders Music Assistant unusable on very old cpus (which also includes the Proxmox default `kvm64`).
> Before updating, please make sure your CPU (virtualized or not) supports the X86_V2 instruction set.
> Proxmox users can most likely just set the processor type to `x86-64-v2-AES`.
> For more information, see https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/5005.

Thank you for your consideration, and for developing such a great project! :)

posts.excerpt:
Hello,

I've started working on a PoC implementing a mechanism that will allow users to block specific tracks or artists so they are automatically skipped during playback. This is particularly useful for provider auto-generated playlists, like radio-generated queues.

Before I finalize the implementation, I wanted to check if this aligns with the project vision and get your input.

Player Behavior:
- Blocked items are silently skipped
- If currently playing item gets blocked → immediate skip
- If no unblocked items remain in queue → graceful stop


**Implementation Plan**

1. Models

    Add blocked: bool = False attribute to:
    - Track dataclass
    - Artist dataclass

2. Server - Database & Controllers

    - Add blocked column to tracks and artists tables
    - Add set_blocked(item_id, blocked) method to TracksController and ArtistsController
    - Update queries to include blocked field

3. Server - API Commands

    Add to MusicController:
    - music/blocked/add_item - Block track or artist
    - music/blocked/remove_item - Unblock track or artist
    - music/blocked/items - List all blocked items

4. Server - Playback Logic
