In my setup (Music Assistant + Snapcast), the audio output is delayed due to buffering and network latency, while lyrics are displayed based on server-side timing. This causes lyrics to appear ahead of the audible audio.

I know that Music Assistant can’t know the exact moment audio reaches the speakers, especially with buffered transports like Snapcast, so perfect sync isn’t realistic.
However, a configurable lyrics timing offset (in ms) would still be very useful.

Ideally:
- a static offset value
- configurable globally and/or per player
- applied only to lyrics rendering

Even an approximate offset would already improve usability a lot in setups with a mostly consistent playback delay.

Thanks!

posts.title: Sonos: Pause and Play from device skips to next queued track. ERROR_PLAYBACK_FAILED in logs.

posts.excerpt:
## The problem

When using `player_queues/play_media` API with `option: "next"` and an Apple Music URI, the **wrong track gets queued**. 

Specifically: `apple_music://track/1737085899` (Shaboozey - A Bar Song Tipsy) resolves to `library://track/347` (Anti-Flag - NVREVR).

Root cause: An orphaned/stale entry in the `provider_mappings` database table incorrectly links the Apple Music ID to the wrong library track.

## How to reproduce

1. Call `player_queues/play_media` via websocket with:
   - `media: "apple_music://track/1737085899"`
   - `option: "next"`
2. Check the queue via `player_queues/items`
3. Queue shows Anti-Flag - NVREVR instead of Shaboozey - A Bar Song

**Additional observations:**
- `option: "replace"` with the same URI works correctly
- `library://track/9648` (same song) with `option: "next"` works correctly
- Other Apple Music IDs for the same library track (1780407617, 1807395565) resolve correctly

## Music Providers

- **Apple Music** - Problem occurs with this provider
- **Spotify** - Not tested with this specific issue
- **filesystem_local** - Works correctly (library:// URIs resolve properly)

## Player Providers

- **Squeezelite** (Nasty Squeezelite) - Prob

posts.excerpt:
**UPDATE:** FYI, those who are newcomers to this feature request discussion thread should know that an initial basic player provider has now been implemented into Music Assistent 2.10 BETA releases and later but it very today experimental so the functionality needs to be both extended and improved to become more usable for those looking to still make full use of their old Bose SoundTouch speakers and receivers.

Suggest add a native "**Bose SoundTouch Player Provider**" inside [Music Assistent server](https://github.com/music-assistant/server/tree/dev/music_assistant/providers) codebase as built-in full featured native [player provider](https://developers.music-assistant.io/#building-your-own-player-provider) component supporting full local media control commands for SoundTouch client player/speaker devices:

* https://www.boselatam.com/en_ar/products/speakers/smart_home/soundtouch_family.html

  * https://bose.fandom.com/wiki/SoundTouch_speakers
  
    * https://bose.fandom.com/wiki/SoundTouch_app

Good timing for this would be now, because Bose has officially opened-up the API documentation for it while at the same time announcing that Bose till sunset this platform but

posts.excerpt:
It has been twenty months since the last poll and so much has changed. MA is up to V2.7 and there have been too many music providers added to list them all!. So it is time to re-do the poll to find out what the Community would like next!

If you would like to discuss these options in more detail then here are the threads. These are in order of the previous vote numbers with new ones added to the bottom so lets see if they stay that way! Do upvote these threads as well as voting here!

Local Audio In https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/1156
Amazon Music https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/626
Emby https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/583
WebDAV https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/526
DLNA https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/890
Pocketcasts https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/3664
Mixcloud https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/2229
YouSee https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/4558

If you want a provider not listed above then open a new feature request and it will be linked above once it starts to get some traction!

posts.title: Severe packet loss playing to Airplay devices

posts.excerpt:
(Version 2.7.3)
Although I'm having a great experience with MA, something showed up today that I haven't seen before. I'm wondering if this is what I think it is... I'm playing a Radio stream to my desktop (Stdo Desktop), when I click the volume I see that it is at 100%. In the attached screenshot it shows the 100% but next to the volume icon it shows 18%. It just so happens that my Windows volume is set to 18% too. Is this how it is supposed to be? Does the volume pop-up show the stream volume (signal path) or is it supposed to reflect my PC volume? When I change the volume on the Player Bar the % value next to the icon does not change.

I know this is oddly specific but I use MA everywhere in my house in all kinds of ways but this is the first time I've seen this when playing to my PC via Sendspin. 

mr.smith

```yaml
action: music_assistant.play_media
target:

data:
  media_type: podcast
  media_id: Tagesschau (Audio-Podcast)
  enqueue: replace
```

  name: Tagesschau (Audio-Podcast)

In principle, they all work perfectly in sync as a group. The only frustrating thing was that they never played the entire playlist. Sometimes it would stop after about 1-10 tracks, and the only way to get it to continue playing was to turn the group off and on again. I have MP3s and AACs in the playlist. Since I disabled Smart Fades two days ago, it finally plays without stopping. I'm documenting this here because I've heard others mention this problem.

### Discussed in https://github.com/orgs/music-assistant/discussions/4610
Originally posted by **ChrisColotti** December 23, 2025 I am not sure if the provider needs an update but as of some of the recent updates every channel played on SiriusXM is clipping when sent to a DLNA player. It's been working for almost a year until recently, the only changes have been HA core and MA updates, the DLNA endpoint hasn't changed. I am not sure what else to try as it was working perfectly fine for so long.
[OzGav](https://github.com/OzGav) Please try with sendspin to the local device @[ChrisColotti](https://github.com/ChrisColotti) That plays fine in the browser so it appears to be a specific combination of SiriusXM with DLNA [OzGav](https://github.com/OzGav) See if you can find some other HLS based streams to try. BBC I believe does. I am interested in whether the DLNA player doesn't like that type of stream @OzGav Great call to test with other HLS streams. They are doing the same thing as SiriusXM, so this would not be an SXM issue it's an HLS stream + DLNA issue that clearly is new and cropped up with recent updates.

posts.excerpt:
Hey there,

I have a quite erratic way of listening to music, and I was wondering if Music Assistant is the right place to customize this.

I'm also open for implementing this through a custom provider (if that's a possible experimental way, without baking this sort of stuff into core).

Perhaps this is also something already provided by scrobblers, but I don't have familiarity with services, so a suggestion would maybe suffice?

## Context: new user / "random" music listener

I'm just getting started with Music Assistant.

I come from YouTube Music, and I heavily rely on the "Like" and "Dislike" feature to shuffle music in my archive/suggestions.

I don't maintain playlists: that's something I'd probably waste months in doing, then never using them.

My daily music listening pattern is "as random as possible, please".

## Likes/Dislikes usage

When listening to a song, I:

* press "dislike" if I want to move forward, and not see it again
* press "like" if a song has to land in my "big bucket of stuff" (could be a default playlist)

## Filtering incoming music by dislikes
 
It would be great if Music Assistant had its own storage for likes/dislikes based

posts.excerpt:
I would like to request support for the Danish music streaming service YouSee Musik.
​It is one of the largest music providers in Denmark (part of the Nuuday group) and is often included in home internet/TV bundles. It is currently integrated into systems like Sonos, which shows that integration is possible.
​Since this is a local provider, I am happy to help with testing or provide any information needed to understand the service's structure.
​Link to service: https://yousee.dk/musik

posts.excerpt: Those of us one crappier Internet connections have difficulty streaming to Music Assistant from Qobuz and other HQ providers. The official Qobuz app allows specifying maximum bit rate/quality when streaming—this option would make Qobuz usable for us when on lower speed Internet connections (or even just when we didn't need a higher quality stream). A configuration option in the Qobuz provider and/or a similar System level one to specify maximum transfer rates for non-local providers would do the trick.

posts.excerpt:
I'm trying the latest nightly to get spotify connect working again (due to https://github.com/music-assistant/support/issues/4393).

Good news that spotify connect works now, however I've noticed that there's no volume control in the spotify app anymore.  It seems that volume control is explicitly disabled in the code:
https://github.com/music-assistant/server/blame/dev/music_assistant/providers/spotify_connect/__init__.py#L479
```python
                "--volume-ctrl",
                "fixed",
```
It seems that this flag has been broken for some time (https://github.com/librespot-org/librespot/pull/1642) so even though `--volume-ctrl fixed` was passed, it still allowed volume control.

Is it intentional to not allow volume control? Can we change it to `--volume-ctrl log` (which is the default) to allow volume changes in the app?

posts.excerpt:
One feature that I really like is the unbiased radio coming through the API. By "unbiased," I mean that somehow the radio mode escapes Spotify's native "echo chamber" that keeps repeating the same songs Spotify thinks you like. For some reason, using Music Assistant, the radio mode provides really great tracks, much better auto-generated playlists than Spotify's native client.

The problem is that using the client ID, we've got no radio; using the token, API rate limits hit hard!

So I was thinking if a hybrid approach could be implemented that would use the token to retrieve the recommendations, keeping the API calls through the client ID for the rest of the functions.

Is this a feasible approach?

2025-11-11 17:42:35.085 DEBUG (MainThread) [music_assistant.spotify_connect] [2025-11-11T13:42:35Z ERROR librespot_discovery] libmdns error: Setting up dns-sd failed: Address in use (os error 98)
2025-11-11 17:42:35.085 DEBUG (MainThread) [music_assistant.spotify_connect] [2025-11-11T13:42:35Z ERROR librespot] Discovery stopped unexpectedly
```

As far as I understood, that's because librespot implemented it's own mDNS stack instead of just registering with Avahi, and I already have another running instance on my host. In normal conditions I'd compile it with another backend, but it's tricky since librespot is already part of the MA container,

Is there some way to change librespot's zeroconf backend inside MA container, since setting it can potentially resolve my issue?

posts.excerpt:
# YouTube

Youtube Music is an experimental Music provider. Google does not provide an official API integration for us to integrate with, so this provider is built on a best-effort basis. We had to jump through A LOT of hoops in order to this to work.

Google is constantly changing things on their end to purposely make it harder for people to pirate videos / music. While we are against piracy, we have to use similar techniques in order to make streaming music from YT Music possible. This means that Music Assistant is also directly affected by Google's changes, now and then breaking the YT Music provider.

Music Assistant has implemented a method to automatically recover from these errors if our upstream friends have implemented a fix. A Music Assistant release is not required. Whenever a fix is available, simply reloading the Youtube Music provider inside Music Assistant is sufficient.

This issue will be updated to reflect the current status of the YT Music provider to keep you updated, so there is no need to post separate issues for this.

## Description
Currently, when I connect **Spotify** as a provider in Music Assistant, all of my favorited albums/artists from Spotify are automatically pulled into the Music Assistant library.  
This causes my **Albums/Artists** views in MA to be cluttered with Spotify items that I don’t want to manage there — I’d like to keep my MA library limited to local files (or other providers), while still using Spotify for playback and search.

## Feature Request
Add a **per-provider option** (e.g. in the provider settings) to control whether *favorites from that provider* are imported into the Music Assistant library. For example:

- ✅ Allow search/playback from Spotify  
- ❌ Do not sync or import favorited albums, artists, playlists, or tracks into the MA library

- Keeps the MA library clean and only containing the content I choose (e.g. local files).  
- Still lets me use Spotify as a playback backend without duplicating my Spotify collection inside MA.  
- Provides more flexibility for users who want to separate their *streaming service favorites* from their *home library*.

I'd like to propose a change to how the footer Play controls bar works throughout Music Assistant.

Currently, the bar operates as a floating island at the bottom of the screen, with the content sliding underneath it, and the scroll bar for the main page content (on desktop) also floating underneath it.

This is problematic for a couple reasons, first the inaccessibility of the scrollbar controls at the bottom of the scrollable area (users cannot click the arrows if their system uses them, or operate the scroll track if it's underneath the play bar). Secondly, it hides content that is underneath it and in some cases makes it less accessible and clickable (I have in some cases navigated to a situation where controls were underneath the playback bar, and I could not use them; I had to resize the window in order to manipulate the UI into making these controls clickable).

Philosophically, the nature of the controls bar being "floating" implies it's more of an ephemeral control, and results in a slightly more complex feel, as content interacts with it underneath and around. This extra complexity isn't really necessary or beneficial, and the difference in look and feel is not all

**Update:** Specification and implementations of Resonate has been renamed to “***Sendspin***” (i.e. “Sendspin Protocol” “Sendspin Server/Client”):

* https://www.sendspin-audio.com/

  * https://github.com/Sendspin/spec

**Update!** Music Assistant server now have built-in native support for Sendspin that is enabled by default as an official technical-preview from the Open Home Foundation and development of its server and client implementations are moving very fast:

* https://www.music-assistant.io/player-support/sendspin/

Not sure if this will be usable on all [ESPHome](https://esphome.io/) based audio output/input devices running on ESP32 (i.e. voice assistants, media player, and smart speaker hardware), but FYI, I heard it sounds like (pun intended) some [Open Home Foundation](https://www.openhomefoundation.org/) and [Music Assistant](https://www.music-assistant.io/) developers have started working on a new experimental open-source Hi-Fi audio streaming protocol for a better multi-room audio and music playback experience on embedded hardware running ESPHome-based client on ESP32 as well as Linux-based client on the roadmap for Raspberry Pi (Zero):

* https://githu

The synchronized lyrics feature does not work correctly for **embedded lyrics** when the lyric text lacks a space between the timestamp (e.g., `[00:00.38]`) and the lyric line.

While I really enjoy using Music Assistant—and now that we have Spotify Connect—it’s still a bit of a shame that Plexamp Headless is not available yet as a plugin provider. The UI of Music Assistant is definitely improving, but to be fair, nothing currently comes close to the Plexamp mobile experience. It would be amazing if Music Assistant players could function as headless Plexamp receivers.

Sure, we can stream our Plex library through Music Assistant, but it’s just not the same as casting directly from the Plexamp app. The mobile experience is truly exceptional.

I’d be very grateful if Plexamp Headless could be implemented as a plugin provider, allowing all players to act as headless receivers for Plexamp, just as with Spotify Connect. I don’t have the technical knowledge to say how feasible that is—it sounds simple in theory, but I imagine there are many technical details I might be overlooking that could make implementation more complex.

Keep up the great work!

### The problem

If a certain song in a playlist is unplayable for some reason, Music Assistant will typically skip it and try the next song. But if an unplayable song is the first song in a Spotify playlist, it will error out and fail to play anything.

Example playlist: https://open.spotify.com/playlist/0LCzBfmaBiOh4K92e2BeJC?si=02b02dccbc7f4419

It was mentioned on Discord that there is a metadata refresh interval set to once every 90 days for artists, albums and tracks, and once every 7 days for playlists. 
This was done a while back when we started getting requests from musicbrainz to limit our lookups.

As all of this done in the background there is no way for the users to know if any of this is happening at all.
Some of that info may be gleaned from logging info, but that only happens when there's critical issues and few users would look at logging info under normal circumstances.

This feature should satisfy the following :

- overall statistics of the media library (total tracks, albums, artists, etc). 
  This info is already available when viewing the pages, but could be listed per provider (if/when available).

- time of last update & time until next planned update
  This allows users to verify the scanning is actually happening. Future iterations could include the option to manually trigger a scan.
  A related feature to 'synchronize now' is available in the provider-settings. However some users may prefer to have features like this available to users who shouldn't have access to the settings themselv

### The problem

If two or more snapcast players are part of a universal group playback will fail. The reason is that the snapcast stream name depends on the queue_id which will be the same for both players. The second player will try to create a stream with a name that already exists, leading to the following error:
```
`2025-04-24 15:55:17.432 WARNING (MainThread) [music_assistant.snapcast] {'code': -32603, 'data': 'Stream with name "Music Assistant - ugpegnamzuq" already exists', 'message': 'Internal error'}`
```

Notes:
- The snapcast provider re-uses existing streams, so we would expect that it wouldn't try to create two with the same name. However, the two streams are created simultaneously, leaving no time to update the list of streams, so the provider does not detect that the stream already exists.
- Even if the stream were re-used by both players it still would be problematic for universal groups with dynamic players. If one of the players is removed from the group i

posts.excerpt:
pacmd is handy to stream sound from one linux to another since it's in most repos and on desktops.
I use it to stream sound from Ubuntu VMs with Spotify to Rpi's connected to speakers all over the house.

The pacmd server runs on the Rpi and the client connects to it via:
pacmd load-module module-tunnel-sink server=SERVERIP:port

It creates a dummy sound card on the client machine.
Sound quality is good (PCM), it's reliable and it doesn't require any extra software besides what's in the distro already.

So Music assistant just needs to invoke the command above to connect to a remote pacmd server.

*On the Rpi side (or any computer connected to the speakers/amp) you run the command bellow to listen to the streams (or use the Pulsaudio extended GUI):
pactl load-module module-native-protocol-tcp port=PORT listen=SERVERIPADDRESS auth-ip-acl='127.0.0.1;CLIENTIP' auth-anonymous=1

SERVERIP=IP of Rpi player
CLIENTIP=IP of the MusicAssistant.

to avoid resampling and reduce CPU load.

I have a homemade whole-home audio system with multiple ALSA output devices and I'd like to playback audio from the pipe like so

```
out=/run/aplay/mydevice.fifo

It would be fantastic to have the ability to specify a local soundcard as an audio output for a player. This feature would effectively turn Music Assistant into a full-fledged open-source wired multi-room audio system.

To elaborate, I have a multi-room audio player from a company called CasaTunes, which is essentially a low-spec PC with two physical soundcards. Each output of these soundcards represents a zone (or room) and acts as an independent player. There are other companies employing the same approach while charging unreasonably high prices for it.

The idea of implementing local players would simply require the ability to specify the device and subdevice, for example:
```-a hw:1,0```

This enhancement would open up new possibilities for multi-room audio setups using wired connections, adding tremendous flexibility for users.

posts.excerpt:
Hi! I'm using Music Assistant in Home Assistant to stream music to a receiver (Onkyo, DLNA). The MA volume slider controls the receiver's volume setting directly, but setting it below 30 is inaudible, and above 60 is dangerously loud. I've had users accidentally change the volume way too high with the slider, as they are accustomed to 0=not audible, 1=barely audible, 100=loud but not deadly. I didn't find any way to change the limits in MA or HA - HA Onkyo DLNA integration lets me set a maximum volume but the setting is not used by MA, and MA's volume normalization can be used to restrict the max volume, but then the receiver needs to be turned very high to hear anything, which is again dangerous when switching to another source. Apologies if this exists or doesn't belong in MA & thanks for the great app!

In summary: a per-output setting that changes what volumes 0 and 100 map to in the volume slider.

posts.excerpt:
So in Spotify when you select a playlist or radio and set it to shuffle or play sequentially you can still add things to the top of the queue in the order they were added or, in the case of an album, in their sequential order. This is helpful if you're just listening to something on shuffle, a song from an album you like comes on, and you want to hear that whole album in order but then automatically go back to the previous playlist.

Currently in MA if you try this with Play Next or Add to Queue with shuffle enabled it will just add the album's tracks and then shuffle them, which is not desired in most cases I'd say. At least that's how I feel as someone who has used the Spotify app for ages.

![Screenshot_20240910_094505_Spotify](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/811d0178-eede-4264-b44b-b228c0cafa64)
In this screenshot here you can see how I've queued up an album which is playing non-shuffled and then once it's done it will just revert back to the playlist I was shuffling beforehand.

posts.excerpt:
As far as I can tell, Music Assistant currently uses ffmpeg's `loudnorm` filter to do loudness normalization. I'm unclear when that calculation is done (on demand? on import?), but it's a relatively cpu-heavy filter to run, and while the loudnorm filter's one-pass support for dynamic normalization (dynamic range compression, effectively) might be useful for radio or podcast streams, the filter is not always appropriate for local music files. (Note that for determining the integrated loudness of local files, ffmpeg's `ebur128` filter should run faster.)

But all of my music files contain pre-calculated "integrated" loudness adjustment information, stored either in the form of [ReplayGain 2.0 tags](https://wiki.hydrogenaud.io/index.php?title=ReplayGain_2.0_specification) or [Opus R128 Gain tags](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7845.html#section-5.2.1). It would be great if Music Assistant could retrieve and use this precalculated loudness normalization information, rather than do its own loudness calculations. (Note that the ReplayGain 2.0 tags use a reference level of -18 LUFS, while the Opus R128 tags use a reference level of -23 LUFS.)

Ideally, the ability to select whether
posts.title: Use ReplayGain (and Opus R128 Gain) tags for loudness normalization

posts.excerpt:
Hi,

I've recently discovered CATT (https://github.com/skorokithakis/catt) and had started writing a web-based media service to allow Google Nest Hub devices to play media file from the local LAN.

Then my husband pointed me to Music Assistant Server and it looked like it could save a lot of time as it has support for both ChromeCast and local and SMB file storage.

The major stumbling blocks, unfortunately, have been:
- recognising media file types -- such as mkv
- transcoding media file types for playback based on the supported media types of the rendering device

CATT provides much wider support - based on ffmpeg, I believe.

With both Music Assistant Server and CATT written in python, I was wondering if there could be any synergistic development between the two projects that would overcome the above (and possibly other) current limitations in Music Assistant Server and speed its development.

Thanks,

-- Peter

posts.excerpt:
Currently, the players in the settings / player list are sorted by alphabetical order.
This is not ideal when there are numerous disabled players,that still show up in the middle of the list. The only way to hide them is to delete the corresponding provider, but that's often not suitable - thus the existence of the "disable" feature on individual players.

I propose a simple change to show two lists, first the enabled players, followed by some separator line, followed by the list of disabled players.
A possible alternative would be some sort of toggle button to switch between the lists of enabled and disabled players.

The next proposal concerns groups. Currently, there is no visual distinction between Airplay groups and other players, for example. This makes them hard to locate in a long player list. The same issue exists for Chromecast groups - one can't tell them apart from individual players.
Universal groups already have their own icon. I'm not sure what the difference should look like. It could be a different background color for the icon. Or there could be a separate column in the view indicating that the device is a group. Or the player type string should include the

posts.excerpt:
Once upon a time, the Google Home app supported casting the Android device device audio to a group of Chromecast devices - or Chromecast audio devices in my case. Then, Sonos sued Google, and they removed this functionality from their app. It still supports redirecting the device audio (or screen), but only to a single Chromecast devices, and no longer to a group.

My main use case is to cast audio from a Youtube music video playing in Firefox with an ad blocker, and casting that to more than one room at a  time, say a whole floor, or the whole house. I'm aware that in this case, the audio and video are out of sync, but that's not a concern at all since I'm not even looking at the screen, and the phone may even be locked while I listen.

It should be noted that even using all-Google software (say, Youtube app, Youtube Music app, or Chrome, and the Google Home app) there is no way to accomplish this, even to a single Chromecast device, let alone a group, as far as I know. The Youtube app can only cast to Chromecast video devices, not Chromecast audio. This is probably due to A/V sync reasons. And the Youtube Music app can only cast audio from specific media designated as audio,

Most music providers currently use a simple favorite or like/dislike system. There are a few that do not, however, and use a star ratings instead .

4. Potentially the file system provider, for file types that support that Metadata

I'm not sure what the support would look like. Star ratings could be exposed through the UI. Or it could be hidden, and there could be some mapping between the two systems, such as 5 stars being equivalent to favorites.

### The problem

Changing the port settings in the slimproto provider is a bit janky. If one of the ports is already occupied it'll give you an error, but still start up the service for the other ports that were not occupied. 

### How to reproduce

1. Make sure you have, for example, port 9000 occupied.
2. Add slimproto as a provider
3. Click save
4. You get an error saying a TCP port might already be occupied
5. Slimproto won't be added as a provider
6. Run `sudo lsof -i -P -n | grep 3483` and you'll see slimproto is still listening on this port
7. Make port 9000 available
8. Save again.
9. You'll get the same error because it won't be able to start listening on 3483 again.
Restarting the docker container fixes this, because it won't start listening on 3483 again on reboot.

### Music Providers

Filesystem and spotify (I don't think it matters)

### Player Providers

Slimproto

### The problem

Nextcloud Music plugin provides subsonic API, but Music Assistant cannot communicate with it because Nextcloud does not provide Subsonic MD5 token-based authentication. (it seems they decided to [use SHA-256 to store the token](https://github.com/owncloud/music/blob/master/lib/Middleware/SubsonicMiddleware.php#L118) instead of MD5, which is broken decades ago. Also, TLS being omnipresent in these days, so "legacy" authentication is no longer a security risk anyway)

### How to reproduce

1. Set up the Nextcloud instance with the music plugin.
2. In Nextcloud Music settings, create a new subsonic credential.
3. Attempt to use that credential on Music Assistant Subsonic Music provider
4. Watch it fail with the "Token authentication not supported" error message.

### Relevant log output

Exposing configuration UI to set value passed to `legacyAuth=[bool]` https://github.com/khers/py-opensonic/blob/master/src/libopensonic/connection.py#46 to user interface will solve the problem.

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2.0.0b88

### The problem

This has been around in at least the last 3 beta versions (since I started testing MA again for v2.0.0b85), and still exists in b88.

If your queues have anything in them, but are NOT playing/connected to speakers (GHome/chromecast in my case), and you send a TTS to a speaker, MA will begin playing back the queue for that speaker or group.

It does this even with Auto Play/Power On disabled. Individual speakers or groups will exhibit the same behavior respectively. The only way to prevent the issue is to completely empty the queue for the device or group. Even then, MA still assumes connection to the speaker after TTS plays and just sits Idle.

Ideally, if MA isn't already playing, it should never connect to and start playback after a TTS, even with Auto Play enabled. 

Of course, if music was already playing and a TTS comes in, it should play the TTS and then resume the music. This functionality DOES work, but perhaps a little too well. 🤣

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

2023.6.0b6

### The problem

When using multiple filesystem entries the removal of some entries does not seem to be handled correctly. 

If the remaining filesystem entries are non-consecutive based on the initial time they were added, for example:

~~1~~2
1~~2~~3
1~~23~~4
1~~2~~3~~4~~

Adding a new filesystem entry will simply replace the last filesystem entry that already exists. So in case of the last example entry 3 is replaced by the new entry.

Restoring the consecutive order or completely removing all entries fixes things, so:

12~~3~~4 Adding replaces entry 4
12~~34~~ Adding creates new entry 3

### How to reproduce

Most AV receivers and renderer support 24 bit audio as Flac or WAV stream.
It would be great to have an option to choose between 16 and 24 bit output and processing to avoid loss in dynamic resolution when volume normalization is active.

@marcelveldt gave some very interesting insights in how audio is handled inside music assistant #1501 :

> All tracks are processed as raw pcm by Music Assistant internally. So everything you play will be first converted to just raw pcm in the sample rate and bit depth of the origin (unless flow mode is enabled) and the gain adjustment is done while extracting the raw source media so the pcm chunks we get into the streaming engine have the gain adjustment applied, that way there should be enough headroom withit the 16 or 24 bits sample rate. ... I settled on applying the correction gain while extracting the raw audio from its base codec. ...
> The final part in the chain is that MA sends either the raw pcm data to the player or encodes it into a codec of the user's choice, by default this is FLAC due to it being lossless while keeping a sane file size ... 

Currently there is an setting for normalization level (EBU) and output codec but no

In the current implementation, every single protocol's scanner returns a distinct playback device entity. This can result in multiple entries for the same device over different protocols, which can be quite annoying in a mixed-protocol environment.

For example, I have a number of Sonos speakers, SOME of them with AirPlay2 support, a number of Apple HomePods, a Samsung soundbar that supports both DLNA and AirPlay2, which is connected to a Philips TV that also supports DLNA, with Chromecast...

The result is a quite noisy list of devices where it's hard to pick which one I want to play on. 

For this reason, I'd like to recommend a merge logic for these speakers.

The first step would be merging ALL devices under the same IP address. If a Sonos speaker responds to both Sonos and DLNA and AirPlay2, don't create three entries, but rather one entry, with a list of protocols supported, and then when playback is initiated, use the most fitting backend.

An additional step would be filtering devices based on name, and if a non-unique name is found, attaching the device model/manufacturer behind it. In my case, both my Apple TV (which has two HomePods in Home Theatre mode connect

### What version of Music Assistant has the issue?

music-assistant/frontend 2.0.11

### The problem

The vuetify config file loaded through the [vite config](https://github.com/music-assistant/frontend/blob/main/vite.config.ts#L22) is currently used to [load the full content](https://github.com/music-assistant/frontend/blob/main/src/styles/settings.scss#L12) of the global.css stylesheet, and the styles from '@egjs/vue3-flicking`. 

It's not intended to do this ([vuetify docs](https://vuetifyjs.com/en/features/sass-variables/#duplicated-css)) as this leads to a copy of these styles being injected into every single component, causing lots of duplicated code.

A preferred solution for loading styles globally would for example be to load them in the [App.vue](https://github.com/music-assistant/frontend/blob/main/src/App.vue) file, or through a css loader configured in vite.

The frontend currently loads ~900KB just stylesheets on the settings page, a lot of which is just duplicated code.

### How to reproduce

Look at any component through your browser's dev-tools and you'll notice, there's the following style defined over and over: 

```css
* {
    -webkit-user-drag: none;

posts.excerpt:
ESPHome's Media Player currently seems to support only MP3 streams. MP3 is a lossy format, sound quality is degraded.
Music Assistant integration by default renders the audio streams in FLAC, which is a lossless format.
Would be nice to enable support in ESPHome for other codecs too:
- lossless FLAC
- uncompressed PCM up to 48k stereo
- open source OPUS (which is lossy, but way better than MP3)
- AAC (also lossy, but better than MP3 and OPUS)

Since only MP3 is supported, one needs to use other firmware than ESPHome, like squeezelite. The goal would be not to have to rely on third party stuff, but remain in the Home Assistant + ESPHome ecosystem.

Adding more codecs of course needs PSRAM for ESP32 (like WROVER module), which is not a problem as plenty of such modules are available. This just needs to be pointed out properly in the documentation.

Also requested in ESPHome FR repo: https://github.com/esphome/feature-requests/issues/1848
posts.title: Support more audio codecs, not just lossy MP3 - in ESPHome

posts.excerpt:
Music Assistant has full support of the "Google Cast" platform and it is in fact one of the preferred solutions to use Music Assistant. The cast platform is used on the Google line-up of speakers such as the Google (Nest) Home and Hub but also a very wide range of other manufacturers adopted the Cast platform such as JBL, Harman Kardon and Sony. So in theory you can have a group of speakers from different brands playing the same music in perfect sync.

**General notes**

- Home Assistant documentation for the cast integration: https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/cast/
- Music Assistant streams audio to the speaker(s) using a local streaming service hosted on TCP port 8095 by default. make sure this port is reachable from your cast speakers on the local network. The IP sent to the speaker is resolved from the "internal URL" field within the Home Assistant configuration. 

**Features:**

- Supports all speakers supported by the cast integration form Home Assistant
- Supports Google cast groups, they will be listed as speaker group in the Music Assistant interface
- Due to the fact that the cast platform has no "power" support, Music Assistant will automatically use

Many Spotify users (including me) have configured and actively are using so-called music scrobbling. Scrobbling is recording the basic details about the song you just listen to like its title, artist or the name of the record and of course the timestamp. Using this kind of service we can generate our database with statistics about the most frequently listened songs, records, and artists accessible for each day, month or any year in the past. If you have local musicfiles (e.g. mp3 or flac files) it is very important that the ID3 tags are correct on your music files. Based on these tags, your music will be loaded into Music Assistant with the correct name, metadata etc.
You can use an ID3 tag editor such as MusicBrainz Picard to correct/set the tags on your music files.
For online music sources (e.g. Spotify) the metadata are retrieved from the music provider(s) itself.

### Basic metadata

- **title**: read from "title" ID3 tag, fallback to filename if the tag is missing.

- **version**: parsed from the title. For example "My great song (live version)" will be parsed as title "My great song" and version "live"

- **track artist(s)**: The Track artist(s) will be read from "artist" ID3 tag. Multiple artists are allowed in that field by a few common separators (e.g. semicolon). If no artist ID3 tag is present, it will try to parse it from the filename (e.g. artist - title.mp3).

- **album title**: The album title will be read from the "album" ID3 tag. A track will NOT be assigned to any album if the album tag is missing. Just like the track title, the version of the album will be parsed from the title.
